pages.title: From take to final mix
pages.caption: A musician doesn’t keep the first take just because it’s finished: record, listen, adjust, record again. That’s the inner loop. The producer’s brief, feedback, quality checks and final approval are the outer loop.

pages.title: Trust the evidence
pages.caption: A confident response from Copilot isn’t validated software. Check the diff in **Changes**, the tests and build in **Terminal**, the running app in **Browser**, and the GitHub checks on the pull request in **Pull requests**.

pages.title: Your judgment, twice
pages.caption: Human judgment applies to both loops. On your machine, you decide whether the diff, tests, build and preview show the change is ready. On GitHub, you review the pull request, its comments and its checks, and decide when it’s ready to merge.

pages.title: A known-good baseline
pages.caption: In a **New worktree** session, select **View** > **Toggle Panel**, then **Terminal**. In `samples/book-app-web`, four passing tests and a build that works are your known-good baseline. Run `npm install` the first time you use each new worktree.
pages.code:
cd samples/book-app-web
npm install
npm test -- --run
npm run build

pages.title: How Copilot gets context
pages.caption: Copilot works from more than your prompt: settings, instructions such as `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, and the repository’s files. More context isn’t always better, so keep each layer focused.

pages.title: Run a snippet
pages.caption: Copy a snippet from Copilot’s reply into the **Terminal** tab, or select **Run** next to it when the reply shows one. The terminal reuses its shell when it can, so your folder and environment carry over between runs.

pages.title: The inner loop
pages.caption: Understand the task, make a focused change, inspect the diff, run the tests and the build, and preview the behavior. If the evidence shows a problem, go round again.

pages.title: Fix a bug from an issue
pages.caption: Select **Create from**, then **Branches**, then `practice-unread-count-bug`, and type `#2` to attach **Keep unread stats correct when filters are active**. Ask for a plan in **Plan** mode, select **Exit plan mode and I will prompt myself** (if the **Review plan** box stays open, select **Continue**), check the mode is **Interactive**, and ask Copilot to implement it. In **Changes**, check that the diff is focused: you can discard a file you didn’t intend, after a confirmation.
pages.code: Use the attached issue as the source of truth. Review @samples/book-app-web/src, identify the root cause, and create a short fix and validation plan.

pages.title: Validate the fix
pages.caption: If Copilot already ran the tests and build, don’t run them twice. Run `npm run dev`, open **Browser** with the **Local** URL, and set **Fantasy** and **Unread** with the search empty: only **The Night Circus** shows, and the unread count is **1** (with the bug, **5**). Stop the server with {key:ctrl+C}.

pages.title: A regression test
pages.caption: A regression test fails with the original bug and passes with the fix. Ask for one that checks the books **Fantasy** and **Unread** show, and the count, then check in **Changes** that it doesn’t weaken an existing expectation.
pages.code: Add or update a focused test that renders the Book App, selects Fantasy and Unread with an empty search field, and confirms that only The Night Circus appears and the displayed unread count is 1. The test should fail with the original bug and pass with the fix.

pages.title: Refactor behind the tests
pages.caption: With the tests passing, you can split `filterBooks` into small, clearly named helpers that keep its behavior. If a test fails, fix the code, not the expected behavior.

pages.title: A second opinion
pages.caption: Type `/` for the slash-command palette and send `/rubber-duck` to critique your diff, tests and browser validation. It uses a different model when a suitable one is available. Without it, choose a different model for the session, or send the same request without the slash command.
pages.code: /rubber-duck Critique this session's diff, tests, and browser validation. What should I double-check before creating a pull request?

pages.title: Pick & Polish
pages.caption: In the browser preview, select **Pick & Polish**, then the empty background of a book card: an `article.book-card` attachment appears in the prompt box. Ask for a small change, then finish with the same diff, test, build and browser evidence.

pages.title: The outer loop
pages.caption: Start from an issue, work in a session, review the diff, open a pull request, answer feedback and failing checks, and merge only when the evidence agrees. Two approval gates are yours, and feedback or a failed check sends the work back to the session.

pages.title: Issues and Pull requests
pages.caption: The **Issues** and **Pull requests** views list the GitHub work that involves you, with tabs such as **Assigned to me** and **Authored by me**. To limit a view to your fork, select the filter icon at the right end of the tab row, select **Query filter mode** (`<>`), and add `repo:YOUR-OWNER/copilot-app-for-beginners` to the existing query, then press `Enter`. Filters belong to the selected view: when you change tabs, check the query and add the `repo:` term again if you need to. Open an item to see its title, repository, number and status.

pages.title: From an issue to a pull request
pages.caption: The issue’s **New session** button starts from `main`, where search already works, so use **Create from** with `practice-search-case-bug` and attach `#1`. Ask for a summary that claims only the checks you saw, select **Create PR**, and don’t merge this practice pull request.
pages.code: Draft a pull request summary for this session. Include what changed, why it changed, and the validation performed. Don't claim a check passed unless it appears in the terminal or CI output.

pages.title: Answer a review comment
pages.caption: Open **Improve empty-state copy** on **Authored by me**, and select **New session** at the top of the pull request. Ask for the smallest useful change, check that it answers the whole comment, then commit, push and confirm the update.

pages.title: Fix a failing check
pages.caption: A **CI check** is an automated validation run on a pull request. Open **Failing stats check practice**, read the failed **Book app web** check, and select **New session**: ask for the smallest fix with your own prompt, and keep the failing test as it is. After you push, the check runs again.

pages.title: Agent Merge
pages.caption: Agent Merge can carry a small, well-scoped pull request through comments, checks and merge rules, and it merges only when GitHub allows. This course doesn’t use it. It’s a finishing aid, not a replacement for human review.

pages.title: Key takeaways
pages.caption: The inner loop happens on your machine, and the outer loop on GitHub. The review panel keeps the diff, terminal and preview in view, tests protect behavior, and the **Issues** and **Pull requests** views connect GitHub work to sessions. A change is ready only when the diff, local validation, GitHub checks and human review agree.

pages.title: Your turn: both loops
pages.caption: Run both loops on a small UI task: Issue 4 on `practice-card-polish`, or, if you did Pick & Polish, the filter row’s labels from `main`. Plan it, build it, inspect the diff, run the tests and build, and preview it wide and narrow. Open a pull request whose summary lists only the checks you ran, and confirm **Book app web** passes.

pages.title: What’s next
pages.caption: Chapter 04 reuses this workflow with a review skill, and builds a custom agent that explains the Book App without editing it.

pages.title: Preview doesn’t update?
pages.caption: Check that the development server runs in this session’s worktree, and that **Browser** uses the **Local** URL shown in **Terminal**.

pages.title: Tests fail in one session?
pages.caption: Check that dependencies are installed in that worktree, and that the session is on the practice branch you expect.

pages.title: Can’t see an issue or pull request?
pages.caption: Check the selected tab and the query’s `repo:` term in the **Issues** or **Pull requests** view, then your repository access, permissions and organization policy.

pages.title: Local and CI disagree?
pages.caption: Compare the Node.js version, the installed dependencies, the branch contents, environment variables and generated files.

pages.title: Pull request still blocked?
pages.caption: Check that required checks ran again, review comments are resolved, and branch protection or merge rules aren’t waiting for another approval.

glossary.definition: The work on your machine: understand, change, inspect, test, build and preview, and repeat when the evidence shows a problem.
The work on GitHub: an issue, a pull request, feedback, checks and a merge.
A view of what changed between two versions of files. In the app, it’s in the review panel’s **Changes** tab.
An automated validation run on a pull request, often through GitHub Actions. CI stands for continuous integration.
Pull request: a GitHub request to review and merge changes from one branch into another.
A test that fails with the original bug and passes with the fix.
`/rubber-duck`: a constructive critic that uses a different model to find missing evidence or assumptions before you open a pull request.
A browser preview tool: pick an element in the running app, and the app attaches it to your next prompt.
A finishing aid that can carry a pull request through comments, checks and merge rules, and merges only when GitHub allows. It doesn’t replace your review.
